correctness.rationale: Gamma integral of h_N gives Laplace profile Phi_N(x)/x with Phi_N=(4x/(1+x)^2)^N; angular integration produces exactly nonnegative Bergman diagonal lambda_n=sum_j Phi_Nj((n+1)/K_j). The h_N L1 mass <=8^N/2 and K_j=M 16^j 8^Nj make sum <=1/(30M)<epsilon. The K_j ratio >=16 bounds lambda_n<=128/15 while lambda_(K_j-1)>=1 at infinitely many distinct indices, so a bounded positive noncompact diagonal operator exists with essential norm>=1. For Berezin B_NK(s) the kernel coefficient m(1-s)^2 s^(m-1)<=4/m, and unimodal mesh bound with ∫Phi_N(x)/x dx =4^N B(N,N)<=4/sqrt N give sup B_NK<=16/sqrt N+12/K. N_j=(j+1)^4 makes these suprema summable, each block compact, so boundary B(s)->0 by dominated convergence. L1 convergence justifies fixed-kernel form interchange but no false operator-norm convergence is used. Independently recomputed exact rational Laplace identities for N=2..7 and x=1/3,1,5/2 and checked beta integrals.

originality.rationale: General positive noncompact Toeplitz examples with vanishing Berezin are prior (Looi 2026). Its compact radial building blocks are translated by nonradial Bergman automorphisms; it explicitly says the radial L1 case remains open, and does not yield a radial final symbol. The present explicit inverse-Laplace construction answers that specific radial-symbol gap, not merely the general phenomenon.
residual_risks: Other older moment-problem counterexamples might provide the same radial L1 symbol construction under a different name.
Do not confuse positivity of Toeplitz operator with positivity of the signed radial symbol; latter would change theorem.
Claim concerns a nonconstructive enormous integer scale but mathematically exact L1 convergence; no uniform pointwise convergence.
